name: Casino Dominican
description: Casino Dominican is a Royal Casino variant played in the Dominican Republic. Picture cards have numerical values (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1/14). Features unique building rules, sweep scoring, and special endgame scoring when nearing 21 points. Played counter-clockwise.

overview.description: Casino Dominican is a Royal Casino variant played in the Dominican Republic. Picture cards have numerical values (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1/14). Features unique building rules, sweep scoring, and special endgame scoring when nearing 21 points. Played counter-clockwise.

history.origins: Casino Dominican is a variant of Royal Casino played in the Dominican Republic. Royal Casino (where picture cards have numerical values) is the standard form in many countries outside Britain and North America. The Dominican version was documented by Humbernio Lockward.
timeline: 18th century: Casino first appears in London and Germany
19th century: Royal Casino variants develop with picture card values
Current: Dominican version played with unique building rules and endgame scoring
history.cultural: Popular in the Dominican Republic. Uses Spanish terms for game actions. Often played socially and in family settings. The game to 21 points with special endgame rules creates exciting finishes.
history.evolution: The Dominican variant differs from Anglo-American Casino in several ways: different building/capturing restrictions, unique sweep scoring, and modified endgame scoring when nearing 21. Counter-clockwise play and Spanish terminology (captura, forma, dejado, pisado) reflect local culture.

setup.players: 2-4 players. 4 players play in fixed partnerships (partners opposite). Deal and play counter-clockwise.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Card values: K=13, Q=12, J=11, 10-2=face value, A=1 or 14 (player's choice).
setup.dealing: First deal: 4 cards to each player, 4 face up to table (separate, all visible). Subsequent deals: 4 cards each, no more table cards. Dealer announces 'last' on final deal. Deal passes to the right.

rules.objective: Capture cards from table layout. First player/team to reach 21 points wins, with special endgame rules.
rules.gameplay: Play counter-clockwise. Must play exactly one card per turn. Three possible uses: Capture (captura/cojer) - take matching card(s) or builds; Build (forma) - combine with table cards into single build (sum=value) or multiple build (sets with same value); Trail - leave card on table. Restrictions: Build owner must hold matching card; Build owner cannot trail (must capture or build more); Cannot trail if played card matches any loose table card (must capture or build); Can capture builds only by matching value; Can increase single build value by adding card (become new owner). Cannot build for partner in partnership game. Cards left capturable called 'dejado' (left) or 'pisado' (stepped). Sweep: clear all table cards (scores bonus).

strategy.basic: Capture cards when possible. Build when you have strong capturing cards. Avoid leaving sweeps for opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played. Use building to secure future captures. Time your sweeps carefully. In partnership game, coordinate with partner's builds.
strategy.advanced: Complex building strategies to deny opponents captures. Force opponents to leave dejado/pisado cards. Endgame strategy when nearing 21: focus on sweeps and guaranteed points (aces, casinos) rather than most cards/spades. Use drifting (intentional non-capture) strategically.
